mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions and potential economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%) indicate persistent inflation without adequate rate hikes, increasing recession risk and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes characterized by high housing starts, the market is typically overbought and prone to correction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods defined by HOUST > 1100 and rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as markets react to weakening supply conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent slowing employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5%) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signal a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to recession concerns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1200 thousand units, it reflects strong consumer demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in sustained growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1200.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive monetary policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.
